text: In Freqtrade, the documented live iteration performs distinct activities, including loading persisted trades, analyzing strategy data, and updating open-order state from the exchange. Treating evidence of one completed activity as evidence of all of them is unsupported; per-stage progress evidence is a monitor design inference from this execution structure. (low confidence)

text: Kubernetes conditions include observedGeneration to identify the desired-state generation behind an observation; the conventions explicitly describe a condition as out of date when that generation lags the current generation. Bot-monitor adaptation: bind status evidence to the configuration revision it actually observed. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: OpenTelemetry supports optional `TraceId` and `SpanId` fields for request and span correlation; if a span identifier is present, a trace identifier should also be present. A bot evidence model can use those fields when the relevant operation has trace context. (low confidence)

text: Historical guidance in Freqtrade issue 7299 uses the timestamp of the last bot cycle as progress evidence and compares its age with an acceptable strategy-specific cycle time; the maintainer notes that a slow strategy can take well over one minute. This is guidance from the thread, not a verified contract for every installed release. (low confidence)

text: Design inference: observe the monitoring transport as a dependency in its own right. Hummingbot documents remote monitoring over asynchronous MQTT channels, and issue 8012 reports repeated bridge reconnect messages that made monitoring and inspection difficult; the issue report does not establish a released fix or a universal strategy failure. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Do not infer a universal healthy value from condition booleans without each condition’s semantics. Kubernetes notes that some conditions are normally true and others normally false, so a generic condition summary cannot be computed without that knowledge. This scopes any proposed single overall bot health indicator. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: A healthy heartbeat does not prove that the service path works. The Gray Failure paper gives an example where the request handler is stuck while heartbeats remain healthy; Google SRE distinguishes internal instrumentation from tests of externally visible behavior. For bot monitoring, retain both perspectives rather than collapsing them into a heartbeat-only health assertion. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Freqtrade issue 11957 is an attributed disagreement rather than a confirmed heartbeat-only failure: the reporter alleged stopped processing, while maintainer xmatthias challenged the inference from missing debug messages and closed the issue because the logs did not establish the problem. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Design inference: keep desired operation separate from observed bot status, and expose multiple named health conditions instead of assuming that a single running label describes every behavior. Kubernetes separates desired intent from status and supports multiple conditions; the gray-failure example shows why process-level health can diverge from useful work. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Design inference: define progress against the work the bot is expected to perform, rather than demanding an arbitrary log message on every heartbeat. Freqtrade documents a repeated loop with candle-scoped work; the disputed issue demonstrates that absence of analysis messages at regular log levels does not establish absence of processing. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: External checks and internal evidence serve complementary purposes: Google SRE says black-box checks expose active symptoms but are poor at predicting imminent problems, whereas white-box instrumentation can expose imminent problems and failures masked by retries. A monitor evidence model should retain the observation method instead of treating these observations as interchangeable. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Kubernetes conditions provide a transferable pattern for incomplete evidence: condition status can be True, False, or Unknown, and an absent condition is interpreted as Unknown. Condition polarity matters, so a generic all-True summary is not valid without knowing each condition meaning. These are Kubernetes conventions, not a pre-existing crypto-bot standard. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Kubernetes condition records distinguish lastTransitionTime, a programmatic reason, and a human-readable message. A bot monitor can adapt that separation so a current condition carries a transition timestamp, a stable reason category, and explanatory detail. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Preserve event time and collection time separately in evidence. OpenTelemetry `Timestamp` is the source-clock event time and may be missing; `ObservedTimestamp` is the collection-system observation time. These fields do not by themselves establish clock synchronization. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: OpenTelemetry supplies a structured evidence vocabulary: Resource describes the emitting source, Attributes describe the specific event, and optional TraceId and SpanId fields associate logs with request processing. A bot-monitor implementation can use these concepts to join observations without assuming every event has trace context. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Design inference: retain evidence history separately from the latest status projection. Kubernetes says historical status information can be lost; OpenTelemetry provides event records with time, source, attributes, and trace context. Neither a latest-status object nor that log schema alone guarantees durable audit retention. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Model desired configuration separately from observed state. Kubernetes distinguishes desired `spec` from current observed `status`; adopting that separation for a bot monitor is an architectural inference, not a bot product guarantee. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Represent each health condition explicitly, including unknown observations. Kubernetes condition `status` can be `True`, `False`, or `Unknown`, and an absent condition means `Unknown`; applying this to bot monitoring avoids interpreting missing evidence as success. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Attach the configuration generation, last transition time, machine-readable reason, and human-readable message to status evidence. Kubernetes defines `observedGeneration`, `lastTransitionTime`, `reason`, and `message` for these roles; a condition based on an older generation can describe obsolete configuration. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model

text: Record evidence provenance and context with distinct fields: OpenTelemetry `Resource` describes the emitting source, `InstrumentationScope` describes the emitting scope, and `Attributes` carries event-specific information. Mapping bot identity and monitor identity onto these roles requires an explicit local convention. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor state and evidence model
